[0] everyday_reading (E): In everyday geometry, square(x, y, r) reads as a square with side r, with (x, y) as a corner. In StdDraw, r is the half-side: the square has side 2r and is centred on (x, y). For circles, r is the radius.
[1] misconception (M) -> SquareArgIsSide: wrong rule: StdDraw.square(x, y, r) draws a square with side length r. Right rule: The square has side length 2r, centred on (x, y).
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> SquareArgIsSide: Points to LT (each shape is centred on (x, y); a polygon joins its points in order and closes back to the first). An uneven trace uses (x, y) as a corner for some shapes, or leaves a polygon open. (here mixing in: "StdDraw.square(x, y, r) draws a square with side length r")

[0] names_the_element (N): Shape commands are StdDraw drawing methods: circle, square and polygon, each with a filled version, plus text and pen color.
[1] states_the_rule (S): A method named after the shape traces its outline, and one whose name begins with filled fills it solid. circle(x, y, r) has radius r and square(x, y, r) has side 2r, both centred on (x, y).

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): polygon(x[], y[]) draws a line from point 0 to point 1, then 1 to 2, and so on, and finally from the last point back to point 0. Each shape is drawn in the pen color current at the call.
[1] output_prediction (OP): square(.2, .8, .1) draws an outline square 0.2 wide with corners (.1, .7) and (.3, .9). filledSquare(.8, .8, .2) draws a solid 0.4-wide square. The methods return void.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): A shape call adds one outlined or filled shape in the current pen color. setPenColor only changes the ink used by later calls (the default is BLACK).

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Shapes use StdDraw's current coordinate scale, pen radius and color, and paint over earlier marks.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Shapes, color and text annotate and highlight drawings, and color can represent data values.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> SquareArgIsSide: Switching shape(...) to filledShape(...) keeps the geometry and only fills it. A diamond is the polygon of a 2r-by-2r square rotated 45 degrees about the same centre.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use circle and square (and their filled versions) for those shapes. For any other shape, use polygon or filledPolygon.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: square's r is the half-length. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Passing the side length as r, so squares come out twice as large and overlap.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: setPenColor takes a Color constant, not a String. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: StdDraw.setPenColor("red"): no method accepts a String (use StdDraw.RED).
